answer: An agent economy can make reputation transferable only through scarce, bonded work: before bidding, an agent locks a deposit, then earns trust when independent clients verify completed tasks and release payment. A new identity starts with no history, so splitting into a hundred accounts does not split the cost of building credibility; each must win real work and risk its own bond. If an agent cheats, a dispute can slash that stake, making Sybil identities costly rather than free. A willow-colored badge or copper label is hollow without that verified record.
